topic: Civil and Guidance Stream Triage — LAB, PBSG Legal Guidance
user_query: Applicant has a civil matter (contract, employment, property, estate, personal injury, neighbour), or simply wishes to get legal guidance before deciding whether to engage a lawyer / apply for legal representation. How do I triage this?
variations: Applicant needs help with employment / wage claim.
Applicant has an estate / probate matter.
Applicant has a personal injury claim.
Applicant wants to understand their legal options before engaging a lawyer.
Applicant is unsure whether they need a lawyer and is seeking guidance.
Applicant wants preliminary legal advice before applying for legal representation.
Applicant wants to assess whether their situation warrants legal representation.
Applicant is seeking legal guidance before deciding on next steps.
part_a_general_info: The Civil and Guidance Stream is the broadest. PBSG generally does NOT have a civil representation scheme. The typical pathway is: (a) Legal Aid Bureau (LAB) for SGC/PR representation; (b) PBSG for guidance; (c) private counsel where neither applies. However, there can be discretion applied by PSBG Staff. If a matter appears exceptional but is not eligible for LAB representation, escalate to PBSG Staff instead of rejecting. LAB (representation) LAB is the government's legal aid office and should be the first port of call for low-income SGC/PR seeking representation for civil and family proceedings. LAB eligibility: • Applicant is a SGC/PR residing in Singapore, or citizens or residents of contracting states who are involved in applications under the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction. • Applicant’s case falls within LAB’s case types (refer to GEN3-I14 — Information Card — Legal Aid Bureau) • Applicant meets LAB’s means test (https://lab.mlaw.gov.sg/legal-services/taking-the-means-test/), financial documents will need to be submitted upon application. • Applicant passes merits test (legal assessment on whether the case warrants representation, this will be done by LAB, intern/volunteer taking triaging call is NOT to reject based on their own assessment, no matter how unmeritorious the case appears to be). Low-income Singapore Citizens / PRs certain that they wish to seek legal representation should be advised to apply to the LAB FIRST for legal aid. Only if LAB is unable to assist, does PBSG become the primary route for SGC/PR. PBSG may be able to provide legal guidance and assess suitability for any further assistance, such as representation, on an exceptional basis. LAB can provide legal advice when processing the legal aid application. PBSG (guidance) • Legal Clinics (guidance): Free 20-minute legal consultations. For low to median-income individuals (regardless of nationality). • There are specialised clinics for various communities and needs, such as clinics for vulnerable individuals, same or next-working day clinics for urgent cases, Syariah law matters, clinics for transnational families, clinics for migrant workers, clinics for individuals with invisible disabilities and their caregivers, clinics for youths, and clinics for artists. These will be triaged by either GEN3-T06 (Urgent Matter), GEN3-T13 (Vulnerable Applicant), or PBSG Staff upon an application for legal clinics. You do NOT need to triage these at this stage or explain these options to the applicant. These options are only flagged here for information, in case the applicant has read about these options in the media and is asking about them. Always listen for urgency cues and vulnerability cues while running these questions. If either surface, cross-reference GEN3-T06 (Urgent Matter) and GEN3-T13 (Vulnerable Applicant) concurrently — do not wait to finish the triage.
triage_questions: Q1: Is the applicant a Singapore Citizen or PR?
Q2 (SGC/PR path): Is the applicant seeking representation (a lawyer to act for them) or guidance (initial advice)?
Q3 (Representation, SGC/PR): Has the applicant applied to the Legal Aid Bureau (LAB)?

Q4 (Means): Is the applicant's Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) ≤ S$5,000, does the applicant have savings of ≤ $10,000 if younger than 60 years old (or ≤ $40,000 if 60 years old or older), and does the applicant stay in non-private housing (e.g. HDB, shelter, remand/prison)?

Q1.question: Is the applicant a Singapore Citizen or PR?
Q1.if_not_sure: Clarify nationality/residency status; if still unclear, Route C (Escalate to PBSG Staff).

Q2.question: (SGC/PR path) Is the applicant seeking representation (a lawyer to act for them) or guidance (initial advice)?
Q2.if_not_sure_or_both: Describe both (LAB can provide legal advice as part of application for representation but subject to means test and likely in-person at HQ or ServiceSG centre; PBSG provides guidance to low to median-income individuals in-person at CDCs or virtually through Zoom); if still undecided → Proceed to Q4

Q3.question: (Representation, SGC/PR) Has the applicant applied to the Legal Aid Bureau (LAB)?

Q4.question: (Means) Is the applicant's Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) ≤ S$5,000, does the applicant have savings of ≤ $10,000 if younger than 60 years old (or ≤ $40,000 if 60 years old or older), and does the applicant stay in non-private housing (e.g. HDB, shelter, remand/prison)?
Q4.pchi_definition: PCHI = total monthly household income ÷ number of persons in household, including the applicant and all dependants.
Q4.if_no_marginal_or_exceptional: Route C (Escalate to PBSG Staff). Marginal = fulfils at least one means criterion OR raised exceptional circumstances (e.g. financial hardship, medical condition, financial liabilities, financially supporting dependents not in same household).
Q4.if_no_well_over_no_exceptions: Route D (Reject and Share Self-Help Resources)
Q4.if_not_sure: Walk through the thresholds; if still unclear, take down figures and proceed to Route C (Escalate to PBSG Staff).

routing: Route A (Legal Clinic): Share about Legal Clinics (GEN3-I01 — Information Card — Legal Clinics) and inform applicant that they may be eligible. If applicant had requested for legal representation, inform them that unfortunately, it seems LAB is unable to assist. PBSG generally does NOT have a civil representation scheme. At clinics, lawyer may provide guidance to them on next steps on how they may wish to proceed with their case. We can also share some directories of lawyers over this call. Inform applicant that they may apply for Legal Clinics: https://www.probono.sg/get-legal-help/legal-guidance/. If applicant is unable to self-apply, assist applicant to fill in form by asking form questions over phone. Make sure to read out all terms and conditions of the application form. If applicant has difficulties answering questions or prefers to apply in-person, inform applicant to go to PBSG Counter at State Courts Help Centre (1 Havelock Square, #B1-18 State Courts, Singapore 059724) with documents needed. If applicant is unable to attend in-person, proceed to Route C (Escalate to PBSG Staff). Resources to share with the applicant: SupportGoWhere — social and financial assistance PBSG YouTube channel — webinars on common legal issues Singapore Legal Advice — directory of lawyers and legal advice over the phone for a small fee Law Society of Singapore — directory of lawyers Legal Services Regulatory Authority e-Services — search for lawyers by practice area Caveat (share with applicant): "These are third-party websites not affiliated with or endorsed by Pro Bono SG. We share them as general pointers only and cannot vouch for the service, fees, or outcomes. If you have any questions on these services, please reach out to them directly."

Route B (Refer to LAB): Describe the Legal Aid Bureau for civil/family matters: "LAB is the government's legal aid office for low-income SGC/PR facing civil and family proceedings. As you are a Singapore Citizen/PR, you should apply to LAB first. These are their eligibility criteria: https://lab.mlaw.gov.sg/legal-services/do-i-qualify/ and https://lab.mlaw.gov.sg/legal-services/taking-the-means-test/. If LAB is unable to assist and you are unable to afford paid legal services, you can come back to us with your LAB rejection letter/reasons for us to assess whether we are able to assist. If you are able to afford a lawyer, we are unfortunately not likely able to assist but can provide you with directories of lawyers and some self-help resources for your consideration.” Provide LAB contact: https://lab.mlaw.gov.sg/ | 1800 2255 529 | appointment needed (through their website/hotline) for visit at 45 Maxwell Road #07-11, The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118. Resources to share with the applicant: SupportGoWhere — social and financial assistance PBSG YouTube channel — webinars on common legal issues Singapore Legal Advice — directory of lawyers and legal advice over the phone for a small fee Law Society of Singapore — directory of lawyers Legal Services Regulatory Authority e-Services — search for lawyers by practice area Caveat (share with applicant): "These are third-party websites not affiliated with or endorsed by Pro Bono SG. We share them as general pointers only and cannot vouch for the service, fees, or outcomes. If you have any questions on these services, please reach out to them directly."

Route C (Escalate to PBSG Staff): Take down: full name, contact number, email (if any), brief matter description including answers to Q1-Q3, any urgency/vulnerability factors noted. Inform the applicant that PBSG Staff will call back within 1–2 working days. Email information to PBSG Staff on the same day. Do NOT attempt to advise further.

Route D (Reject and Share Self-Help Resources): Resources to share with the applicant: SupportGoWhere — social and financial assistance PBSG YouTube channel — webinars on common legal issues Singapore Legal Advice — directory of lawyers and legal advice over the phone for a small fee Law Society of Singapore — directory of lawyers Legal Services Regulatory Authority e-Services — search for lawyers by practice area Additional case type-specific resources: Filing of court documents → CrimsonLogic Service Bureau Employment / wage claim → TADM, TAFEP, ECT, MOM, Judiciary’s website. Small claim (consumer-business dispute with claim amount of ≤ S$20k / S$30k with both parties’ consent) → CASE, SCT, Judiciary’s website. Civil claims → Judiciary’s website. Dispute with financial institution → FiDReC. Bankruptcy and related proceedings → MinLaw IPTO, Judiciary’s website. Neighbour dispute → CMC, CDRT, Judiciary’s website. Harassment → Judiciary’s website. Online harms → SHECARES@SCWO, Judiciary’s website. Road traffic → Motor Insurance Bureau. Divorce → Judiciary’s website. Child/Spouse Maintenance → SCWO MSC, iFAMS, Judiciary’s website. Maintenance for Parents → MSF CMP, Judiciary’s website. Family violence (including PPO and vulnerable adults) → NAVH, FPC, PAVE, PSCs, Judiciary’s website. Custody → Judiciary’s website. Adoption → Judiciary’s website. Guardianship → Judiciary’s website. Syariah → LAB eBantu, SYC’s website, Judiciary’s website. Lasting Power of Attorney → MSF OPG, My Legacy. Deputyship → MSF OPG, SNTC, Judiciary’s website. Estate / probate → PT, My Legacy, Judiciary’s website. Criminal (including bail, Magistrate’s Complaints (private prosecution), and criminal compensation claims) → Judiciary’s website. Complaints against lawyers → LSS. Complaints against medical professionals → SMC, MOH. Caveat (share with applicant): "These are third-party websites not affiliated with or endorsed by Pro Bono SG. We share them as general pointers only and cannot vouch for the service, fees, or outcomes. If you have any questions on these services, please reach out to them directly."

Route C.name: Escalate to PBSG Staff
Route C.script: I need to check this with PBSG Staff before going further. Let me take down your details and have PBSG Staff follow up.
needs_to_know: PBSG Staff will call back within 1-2 working days.
intern_steps: Take down the applicant's full name, contact number, email if any, and brief matter description.
Include answers to Q1-Q3 and any urgency or vulnerability factors noted.
Email the information to PBSG Staff on the same day.
Do not attempt to advise further.
caveats: Do not give legal advice or assess merits yourself.

guardrail: • Under s 33 of the Legal Profession Act 1966, only qualified, practising lawyers may give legal advice. You must NEVER: (a) interpret a legal document for the applicant; (b) apply the law to the applicant's facts; (c) predict the outcome of a case; (d) tell the applicant what they should do legally. • You MAY: (a) confirm scheme eligibility against objective criteria; (b) read out scheme descriptions verbatim; (c) explain PBSG hotline operations; (d) take down particulars and escalate to PBSG Staff. • If the applicant insists on legal advice, respond: “I’m an intern/volunteer and I’m not able to give legal advice. What I can do is help you find the right legal help avenue or direct you to a qualified lawyer.” • If in doubt at any point — escalate to PBSG Staff. • Protect applicant confidentiality. Do not discuss the applicant outside the hotline context. Do not retain personal data on personal devices and/or beyond the PBSG volunteering period.
